critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1400 lines — extract routers (auth, rbac, integrations, channels, helpdesk, invitations, tickets) into /app/backend/routers/ before next round. Already flagged in iterations 2 & 3.

PATCH /api/tickets/{tid}/assign uses require_permission('tickets.write') but does NOT scope to owner_id — any user with tickets.write can re-assign ANY ticket in any workspace. Add owner_id check or workspace scoping.
GET /api/tickets/{tid}/* endpoints (PUT, comments, delete) scope by owner_id, but the new /assign does not. Inconsistency to fix.

_auto_assign() updates `assignment.last_assigned_index` globally on the singleton helpdesk_config doc — this means round-robin index is shared across ALL workspaces (no multi-tenant isolation). Same for SLA config. Fine for single-tenant but should be per-owner_id when going multi-tenant.
Last-admin guard counts admins globally (db.users.count_documents({'role':'admin'})). In a multi-tenant system this should be scoped per workspace. For single-tenant demo this is acceptable.

Invitation token uses uuid4 — fine entropy-wise, but the invite check endpoint reveals email + role even before accept. Consider rate limiting /invitations/check/{token} to prevent token enumeration (though uuid space makes this academic).
Helpdesk config singleton pattern (db.helpdesk_config.find_one({})) means there is exactly ONE config across the whole DB — confirm this is intentional vs per-owner.
TicketIn.custom: dict accepts arbitrary keys with no validation against ticket-fields collection — a misconfigured client can store anything. Consider validating keys against active ticket_fields.
Comments are stored as embedded array in tickets — fine for small N, but at >100 comments per ticket Mongo doc size becomes an issue. Future: move comments to its own collection.
/api/groups GET is open to any authenticated user but POST/DELETE require settings.manage — consistent. /api/canned-responses is per-owner (good).
